summary: Implement conditional Slack channel claim flow with TTL retention and Confluence seed + optional Jira project orchestration
description:
Issue summary: Request to build a conditional channel-claim automation that: (1) exposes a lightweight Slack 'Claim' button for ephemeral project channels, (2) when claimed creates a templated Confluence seed page and optionally provisions a scoped Jira project, and (3) applies a configurable TTL retention policy that auto-archives or marks channel for review when expiry reached.

Impact: Currently teams manually claim ephemeral channels and create associated docs; channels either remain orphaned or get prematurely archived. This automation reduces orphaned channels, enforces retention guardrails, and ensures discoverability (seeded Confluence page). Helps compliance and on-call handoff for experiments.

Environment: Production Slack workspace (redwood-prod), Confluence (prod), Jira (prod). Primary scope: public and private ephemeral channels created by self-service pod bootstrapping.

Request details:
- Add a Slack workflow button (or message action) "Claim channel" that opens a small modal: owner, team, expected TTL (7/30/90 days), opt-in for Jira project creation.
- On claim: create Confluence seed page from a template (metadata: channel-name, owner, claim-date, TTL), tag page with 'ephemeral-claimed', and post link to channel.
- If Jira project requested: call existing provisioning webhook to create a lightweight project with restricted permissions and link project key in Confluence.
- TTL enforcement: scheduled job evaluates claimed channels; for channels approaching TTL-7d send reminder DM to owner; at TTL expiry automatically archive channel or mark for retention-review (based on channel policy).
- Audit: write claim, reminders, archive actions to central audit log (Confluence page comment + centralized log file + optional S3 export).

Acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and runbook details below.
steps_to_reproduce: Create an ephemeral channel via pod bootstrap template in prod Slack.
Observe current manual process: post a pinned message asking for an owner and create docs manually.
Attempt to locate existing Confluence seed - none exists by default.
There is no TTL-based scheduled reviewer flow tied to owner reminders.
Goal: after automation is deployed a new "Claim channel" action appears and follows the flow below.
acceptance_criteria: A Claim button appears in ephemeral channels and opens modal capturing owner, TTL, and Jira opt-in.
Confluence seed page created within 30s of claim and linked back to channel in a confirmation message.
If Jira opt-in selected, a sandbox Jira project is provisioned and project key posted in Confluence and Slack within 2 minutes.
Scheduler sends owner reminders at TTL-7d and TTL-1d; archive action at TTL expiry executes with audit entry.
Audit entries include: actor, channel, TTL chosen, timestamps, and linked Confluence/Jira artifacts.
Permissions: Confluence page uses template and inherits team visibility controls; Jira project respects self-service guardrails.

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary - internal tools): deploy to dev and a single engineering pod workspace for 1 week; validate claim->Confluence creation and audit logging.
Phase 2 (staged): enable for 3 additional pods and enable TTL reminders; monitor for false archives for 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (wide): enable for all ephemeral channel templates; enable Jira opt-in for enterprise pods only.
Rollback: disable Claim action via feature flag and run reverse job to un-archive any channels archived in error within 48 hours; maintain manual override in runbook.
related_workflow_requirements: Slack app scopes required: channels:manage, channels:read, chats:write, users:read, reactions:write, chat:write.customize, workflows:triggers
Confluence API: template-create, page-create, label-create (use service account with page-create scope only)
Jira provisioning webhook: idempotent create, return project key, ensure RBAC mapping
Scheduler: cron job in infra with visibility to audit S3 or central logging sink
Audit: log to central Loki/ELK plus Confluence comment for easy human discoverability
testing_checklist: Unit tests for modal payload validation (owner email, TTL values)
E2E test in staging: claim -> Confluence page exists -> optional Jira project created -> TTL scheduler triggers on simulated time
Load test: simulate 500 concurrent claims to validate webhook backoff
Security review: confirm service account minimal scopes and token rotation policy
UX sanity: modal localized text and mobile layouts verified
